text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Swedish non-governmental group has arranged inter-party talks between Zambia's ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy and the opposition, to discuss disputes arising from last November's general elections. The talks are to be held in Stockholm on Tuesday.
- The government has advised health workers to re-apply for their jobs as the central health board is given autonomy from the government.

- Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa Secretary-General Erastus Mwencha says the regional grouping's vision for an African economic community will succeed because it has the backing of the continent's regional groupings.
- Fifty Cuban specialist doctors recruited by the Zambian government are expected to arrive in the country this month.
- Western diplomats say Zambia is not yet ready for a Consultative Group meeting set for early July as it has not addressed donors' main concerns.
